messages.text: Haskell backs Borthwick, Pollock as England prepare for Nations Championship

metadata.summary: James Haskell has backed Steve Borthwick as "the right man for the job" as England prepare for the conclusion of the inaugural Nations Championship in November.
metadata.content: England Rugby: Steve Borthwick and Henry Pollock backed by James Haskell ahead of Nations Championship fixtures | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England Rugby: Steve Borthwick and Henry Pollock backed by James Haskell ahead of Nations Championship fixtures James Haskell believes Steve Borthwick is the right man to lead England at the 2027 Rugby World Cup and shares his excitement over rising star Henry Pollock ahead of November's Nations Championship fixtures against Australia, Japan and New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham By Matthew Wolfe Monday 2 November 2026 06:01, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England head coach Steve Borthwick says that contract extension hasn't changed the focus on 2027 World Cup James Haskell has backed Steve Borthwick as "the right man for the job" as England prepare for the conclusion of the inaugural Nations Championship in November. Borthwick oversaw England's worst-ever Six Nations campaign earlier this year, with four losses from their five matches, but despite growing pressure the RFU have publicly expressed their support for Borthwick through to the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia. This month, England will face Australia, Japan and New Zealand ahead of Finals Weekend, which takes place November 27-28 at Twickenham. Former England international Haskell, who earned 77 Test caps between 2007 and 2019, insists it is not the time to change the head coach. Nations Championship: Schedule

messages.text: Hamilton hits out at Leclerc after Mexico clash

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton criticised Charles Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix, suggesting his team-mate's driving came down to "a mentality thing".
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton hits out at Charles Leclerc after Ferrari drivers' Mexico City GP clash as he questions team-mate's approach | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton hits out at Charles Leclerc after Ferrari drivers' Mexico City GP clash as he questions team-mate's approach Ferrari drivers' lap-one squabble effectively lost them the race to Red Bull's Max Verstappen; Hamilton says of Leclerc: "I don't think it's an age thing. I think it's a mentality thing"; watch every session of the Sao Paulo GP from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Monday 2 November 2026 09:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was left furious after Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc overtook him on the opening lap while leaving the track but was only given a five-second penalty for the infringement. Lewis Hamilton criticised Charles Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix, suggesting his team-mate's driving came down to "a mentality thing". Hamilton and Leclerc battled for the lead during the first four corners of Sunday's race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in a duel that saw the latter cut across the second chicane to take over first place from the pole-sitting Briton. Having also run slightly wide himself in defence of the position, Hamilton was overtaken on the exit of Turn Five by Max Verstappen. messages.text: Antonelli: I couldn't see through my tears on title-clinching lap

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli says he "couldn't see" through his tears on the final lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix as he was overcome with emotion before becoming Formula 1 world champion for the first time.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli becomes F1 world champion: Mercedes driver says he couldn't see through his tears on final lap of Mexico City GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Kimi Antonelli becomes F1 world champion: Mercedes driver says he couldn't see through his tears on final lap of Mexico City GP Kimi Antonelli has revealed he was overcome with emotion during the closing stages of the Mexico City Grand Prix, which he finished third in to seal the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship; watch every session of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Monday 2 November 2026 08:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli watches back a montage of videos from his journey from go-karting, to F1's youngest champion Kimi Antonelli says he "couldn't see" through his tears on the final lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix as he was overcome with emotion before becoming Formula 1 world champion for the first time. Antonelli finished third behind race-winner Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to lower Sebastian Vettel's record of being F1's youngest world champion by over three years, sealing the title at 20 years and 68 days old. The Italian was overcome with emotion on team radio and in several post-race interviews, and revealed he was already crying during the closing stages of the race. metadata.summary: Not since 2012 - when current boss Mikel Arteta was commanding Arsenal's midfield on the pitch - had the Gunners won on Liverpool’s patch. That curse has finally been broken.
metadata.content: Arsenal's 'defensive masterclass' praised in Liverpool win as Jamie Carragher salutes 'world class' Declan Rice | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Arsenal's 'defensive masterclass' praised in Liverpool win as Jamie Carragher salutes 'world class' Declan Rice Arsenal eked out a first victory at Anfield for 14 years by beating Liverpool 1-0 thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half winner; Jamie Carragher called their defensive performance outstanding and reserved special praise for Declan Rice Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Monday 2 November 2026 09:07, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daniel Sturridge heaps praise on Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta for what he's built with the Gunners and says his system is 'almost perfect'. Not since 2012 - when current boss Mikel Arteta was commanding Arsenal's midfield on the pitch - had the Gunners won on Liverpool’s patch. That curse has finally been broken. Winning at Anfield is a rarity, especially for Arsenal. But Arteta's side were ruthless at both ends of the pitch, a tactical triumph for the boss and one that underlines his side's champion mentality. "I love when there is something that we haven't done for many years," beamed the Spaniard, who praised his players for a defensive performance he called "remarkable".
